title: Wheatstone bridge and meter bridge
notes: This is the same bridge with the classroom names written out. P and Q may be the ratio arms of a box, while R is known and S is the unknown. Balance is still P/Q = R/S.
When the ratio arms are the wire, P is proportional to the left length and Q to the right length. A jockey at the centre means the two gaps are equal if the wire is uniform.
If the balance point is far toward one end, the percentage uncertainty in the short length is large. Changing the known resistor to bring the balance near 50 cm is good practice.
The battery key is closed before the galvanometer key, and opened in the reverse order, so that a self-induced kick does not throw the galvanometer.
The unknown can be a coil whose resistance changes with temperature. The bridge then measures that temperature effect, provided the wire itself stays cool.
A small series resistor added to one gap shifts the balance in a predictable direction. That shift is a check that the lengths have been assigned the right way.
